blocks.text:
DEST="$SDK_ROOT/$VER"

        # gh-1736: the archive is picked per HOST arch — the arch-less
        # flutter_macos_<v>-stable.zip is the X64 build, and an x64 dart
        # cannot exec on this Apple-silicon runner ("Bad CPU type in
        # executable", exit 126). Both matrix legs run on this ONE host
        # and share the slot (the matrix arch only steers
        # FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS), so the slot's SDK must match uname -m.
        # Same resolution subosito/flutter-action performs from the
        # platform arch; the naming lives in the tested sdk_slot.py.
        HOST_ARCH="$(uname -m)"
        ARCHIVE="$(python3 "$SLOT" archive "$VER" "$HOST_ARCH")"
        echo "host arch $HOST_ARCH -> $ARCHIVE"

        # Self-heal before trusting a non-INSTALL verdict: a marker can
        # point at a version dir that a human or disk cleanup removed.
        # Without this the SKIP path would export a PATH entry with no
        # flutter binary under it and every later step would die at
        # `flutter --version` until someone deletes the marker by hand —
        # the brick the #357 review flagged on the old swap. gh-1736
        # adds the arch half: a slot unpacked from a wrong-arch archive
        # (or unstamped, like the poisoned runner slot this fixes) is
        # pruned by ensure_arch and reinstalled from the right archive.
        if [[ "$DECISION" != INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ ! -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER is missing from $SDK_ROOT — reinstalling"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          elif [[ "$(python3 "$SLOT" ensure_arch "$DEST" "$HOST_ARCH")" == reinstall* ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER at $DEST is not usable on $HOST_ARCH — reinstalling from the correct archive"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          fi
        fi

        if [[ "$DECISION" == INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "Flutter $VER already installed by a concurrent leg — reusing it"
          else
            echo "Downloading Flutter $VER (spec: $SPEC, host $HOST_ARCH) — one-time per pinned version..."
            STAGE="$(mktemp -d "$SDK_ROOT/.stage.XXXXXX")"
            # --max-time bounds EACH transfer, --retry-max-time bounds
            # the whole retry cycle: a wedged ~1GB download can never
            # hang the job until GitHub's ceiling kills it. (Same
            # pattern as the bounded asset downloads in build-macos.)
            if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
                --max-time 600 --retry-max-time 900 \
                -o "$STAGE/flutter.zip" \
                "https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/releases/stable/macos/$ARCHIVE"; then
              echo "::error::Flutter SDK download for $ARCHIVE failed after retries (bounded: --max-time 600 per attempt, --retry-max-time 900 total). The runner's network or storage.googleapis.com is unhealthy — check and re-run; partial state stayed inside $STAGE only, the pinned slot is untouched."
              exit 1
            fi
            unzip -q "$STAGE/flutter.zip" -d "$STAGE"
            # Stamp the staged tree with the host arch BEFORE the
            # slot-in (gh-1736): ensure_arch can later tell a healthy
            # slot from a wrong-arch one and self-heal it instead of
            # re-exporting an unrunnable SDK on every run.

restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

blocks.text:
DEST="$SDK_ROOT/$VER"

        # gh-1736: the archive is picked per HOST arch — the arch-less
        # flutter_macos_<v>-stable.zip is the X64 build, and an x64 dart
        # cannot exec on this Apple-silicon runner ("Bad CPU type in
        # executable", exit 126). Both matrix legs run on this ONE host
        # and share the slot (the matrix arch only steers
        # FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS), so the slot's SDK must match uname -m.
        # Same resolution subosito/flutter-action performs from the
        # platform arch; the naming lives in the tested sdk_slot.py.
        HOST_ARCH="$(uname -m)"
        ARCHIVE="$(python3 "$SLOT" archive "$VER" "$HOST_ARCH")"
        echo "host arch $HOST_ARCH -> $ARCHIVE"

        # Self-heal before trusting a non-INSTALL verdict: a marker can
        # point at a version dir that a human or disk cleanup removed.
        # Without this the SKIP path would export a PATH entry with no
        # flutter binary under it and every later step would die at
        # `flutter --version` until someone deletes the marker by hand —
        # the brick the #357 review flagged on the old swap. gh-1736
        # adds the arch half: a slot unpacked from a wrong-arch archive
        # (or unstamped, like the poisoned runner slot this fixes) is
        # pruned by ensure_arch and reinstalled from the right archive.
        if [[ "$DECISION" != INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ ! -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER is missing from $SDK_ROOT — reinstalling"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          elif [[ "$(python3 "$SLOT" ensure_arch "$DEST" "$HOST_ARCH")" == reinstall* ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER at $DEST is not usable on $HOST_ARCH — reinstalling from the correct archive"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          fi
        fi

        if [[ "$DECISION" == INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "Flutter $VER already installed by a concurrent leg — reusing it"
          else
            echo "Downloading Flutter $VER (spec: $SPEC, host $HOST_ARCH) — one-time per pinned version..."
            STAGE="$(mktemp -d "$SDK_ROOT/.stage.XXXXXX")"
            # --max-time bounds EACH transfer, --retry-max-time bounds
            # the whole retry cycle: a wedged ~1GB download can never
            # hang the job until GitHub's ceiling kills it. (Same
            # pattern as the bounded asset downloads in build-macos.)
            if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
                --max-time 600 --retry-max-time 900 \
                -o "$STAGE/flutter.zip" \
                "https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/releases/stable/macos/$ARCHIVE"; then
              echo "::error::Flutter SDK download for $ARCHIVE failed after retries (bounded: --max-time 600 per attempt, --retry-max-time 900 total). The runner's network or storage.googleapis.com is unhealthy — check and re-run; partial state stayed inside $STAGE only, the pinned slot is untouched."
              exit 1
            fi
            unzip -q "$STAGE/flutter.zip" -d "$STAGE"
            # Stamp the staged tree with the host arch BEFORE the
            # slot-in (gh-1736): ensure_arch can later tell a healthy
            # slot from a wrong-arch one and self-heal it instead of
            # re-exporting an unrunnable SDK on every run.

restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

blocks.text:
DEST="$SDK_ROOT/$VER"

        # gh-1736: the archive is picked per HOST arch — the arch-less
        # flutter_macos_<v>-stable.zip is the X64 build, and an x64 dart
        # cannot exec on this Apple-silicon runner ("Bad CPU type in
        # executable", exit 126). Both matrix legs run on this ONE host
        # and share the slot (the matrix arch only steers
        # FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS), so the slot's SDK must match uname -m.
        # Same resolution subosito/flutter-action performs from the
        # platform arch; the naming lives in the tested sdk_slot.py.
        HOST_ARCH="$(uname -m)"
        ARCHIVE="$(python3 "$SLOT" archive "$VER" "$HOST_ARCH")"
        echo "host arch $HOST_ARCH -> $ARCHIVE"

        # Self-heal before trusting a non-INSTALL verdict: a marker can
        # point at a version dir that a human or disk cleanup removed.
        # Without this the SKIP path would export a PATH entry with no
        # flutter binary under it and every later step would die at
        # `flutter --version` until someone deletes the marker by hand —
        # the brick the #357 review flagged on the old swap. gh-1736
        # adds the arch half: a slot unpacked from a wrong-arch archive
        # (or unstamped, like the poisoned runner slot this fixes) is
        # pruned by ensure_arch and reinstalled from the right archive.
        if [[ "$DECISION" != INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ ! -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER is missing from $SDK_ROOT — reinstalling"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          elif [[ "$(python3 "$SLOT" ensure_arch "$DEST" "$HOST_ARCH")" == reinstall* ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER at $DEST is not usable on $HOST_ARCH — reinstalling from the correct archive"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          fi
        fi

        if [[ "$DECISION" == INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "Flutter $VER already installed by a concurrent leg — reusing it"
          else
            echo "Downloading Flutter $VER (spec: $SPEC, host $HOST_ARCH) — one-time per pinned version..."
            STAGE="$(mktemp -d "$SDK_ROOT/.stage.XXXXXX")"
            # --max-time bounds EACH transfer, --retry-max-time bounds
            # the whole retry cycle: a wedged ~1GB download can never
            # hang the job until GitHub's ceiling kills it. (Same
            # pattern as the bounded asset downloads in build-macos.)
            if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
                --max-time 600 --retry-max-time 900 \
                -o "$STAGE/flutter.zip" \
                "https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/releases/stable/macos/$ARCHIVE"; then
              echo "::error::Flutter SDK download for $ARCHIVE failed after retries (bounded: --max-time 600 per attempt, --retry-max-time 900 total). The runner's network or storage.googleapis.com is unhealthy — check and re-run; partial state stayed inside $STAGE only, the pinned slot is untouched."
              exit 1
            fi
            unzip -q "$STAGE/flutter.zip" -d "$STAGE"
            # Stamp the staged tree with the host arch BEFORE the
            # slot-in (gh-1736): ensure_arch can later tell a healthy
            # slot from a wrong-arch one and self-heal it instead of
            # re-exporting an unrunnable SDK on every run.

restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

blocks.text:
DEST="$SDK_ROOT/$VER"

        # gh-1736: the archive is picked per HOST arch — the arch-less
        # flutter_macos_<v>-stable.zip is the X64 build, and an x64 dart
        # cannot exec on this Apple-silicon runner ("Bad CPU type in
        # executable", exit 126). Both matrix legs run on this ONE host
        # and share the slot (the matrix arch only steers
        # FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS), so the slot's SDK must match uname -m.
        # Same resolution subosito/flutter-action performs from the
        # platform arch; the naming lives in the tested sdk_slot.py.
        HOST_ARCH="$(uname -m)"
        ARCHIVE="$(python3 "$SLOT" archive "$VER" "$HOST_ARCH")"
        echo "host arch $HOST_ARCH -> $ARCHIVE"

        # Self-heal before trusting a non-INSTALL verdict: a marker can
        # point at a version dir that a human or disk cleanup removed.
        # Without this the SKIP path would export a PATH entry with no
        # flutter binary under it and every later step would die at
        # `flutter --version` until someone deletes the marker by hand —
        # the brick the #357 review flagged on the old swap. gh-1736
        # adds the arch half: a slot unpacked from a wrong-arch archive
        # (or unstamped, like the poisoned runner slot this fixes) is
        # pruned by ensure_arch and reinstalled from the right archive.
        if [[ "$DECISION" != INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ ! -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER is missing from $SDK_ROOT — reinstalling"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          elif [[ "$(python3 "$SLOT" ensure_arch "$DEST" "$HOST_ARCH")" == reinstall* ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER at $DEST is not usable on $HOST_ARCH — reinstalling from the correct archive"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          fi
        fi

        if [[ "$DECISION" == INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "Flutter $VER already installed by a concurrent leg — reusing it"
          else
            echo "Downloading Flutter $VER (spec: $SPEC, host $HOST_ARCH) — one-time per pinned version..."
            STAGE="$(mktemp -d "$SDK_ROOT/.stage.XXXXXX")"
            # --max-time bounds EACH transfer, --retry-max-time bounds
            # the whole retry cycle: a wedged ~1GB download can never
            # hang the job until GitHub's ceiling kills it. (Same
            # pattern as the bounded asset downloads in build-macos.)
            if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
                --max-time 600 --retry-max-time 900 \
                -o "$STAGE/flutter.zip" \
                "https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/releases/stable/macos/$ARCHIVE"; then
              echo "::error::Flutter SDK download for $ARCHIVE failed after retries (bounded: --max-time 600 per attempt, --retry-max-time 900 total). The runner's network or storage.googleapis.com is unhealthy — check and re-run; partial state stayed inside $STAGE only, the pinned slot is untouched."
              exit 1
            fi
            unzip -q "$STAGE/flutter.zip" -d "$STAGE"
            # Stamp the staged tree with the host arch BEFORE the
            # slot-in (gh-1736): ensure_arch can later tell a healthy
            # slot from a wrong-arch one and self-heal it instead of
            # re-exporting an unrunnable SDK on every run.

restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

DEST="$SDK_ROOT/$VER"

        # gh-1736: the archive is picked per HOST arch — the arch-less
        # flutter_macos_<v>-stable.zip is the X64 build, and an x64 dart
        # cannot exec on this Apple-silicon runner ("Bad CPU type in
        # executable", exit 126). Both matrix legs run on this ONE host
        # and share the slot (the matrix arch only steers
        # FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS), so the slot's SDK must match uname -m.
        # Same resolution subosito/flutter-action performs from the
        # platform arch; the naming lives in the tested sdk_slot.py.
        HOST_ARCH="$(uname -m)"
        ARCHIVE="$(python3 "$SLOT" archive "$VER" "$HOST_ARCH")"
        echo "host arch $HOST_ARCH -> $ARCHIVE"

        # Self-heal before trusting a non-INSTALL verdict: a marker can
        # point at a version dir that a human or disk cleanup removed.
        # Without this the SKIP path would export a PATH entry with no
        # flutter binary under it and every later step would die at
        # `flutter --version` until someone deletes the marker by hand —
        # the brick the #357 review flagged on the old swap. gh-1736
        # adds the arch half: a slot unpacked from a wrong-arch archive
        # (or unstamped, like the poisoned runner slot this fixes) is
        # pruned by ensure_arch and reinstalled from the right archive.
        if [[ "$DECISION" != INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ ! -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER is missing from $SDK_ROOT — reinstalling"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          elif [[ "$(python3 "$SLOT" ensure_arch "$DEST" "$HOST_ARCH")" == reinstall* ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER at $DEST is not usable on $HOST_ARCH — reinstalling from the correct archive"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          fi
        fi

        if [[ "$DECISION" == INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "Flutter $VER already installed by a concurrent leg — reusing it"
          else
            echo "Downloading Flutter $VER (spec: $SPEC, host $HOST_ARCH) — one-time per pinned version..."
            STAGE="$(mktemp -d "$SDK_ROOT/.stage.XXXXXX")"
            # --max-time bounds EACH transfer, --retry-max-time bounds
            # the whole retry cycle: a wedged ~1GB download can never
            # hang the job until GitHub's ceiling kills it. (Same
            # pattern as the bounded asset downloads in build-macos.)
            if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
                --max-time 600 --retry-max-time 900 \
                -o "$STAGE/flutter.zip" \
                "https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/releases/stable/macos/$ARCHIVE"; then
              echo "::error::Flutter SDK download for $ARCHIVE failed after retries (bounded: --max-time 600 per attempt, --retry-max-time 900 total). The runner's network or storage.googleapis.com is unhealthy — check and re-run; partial state stayed inside $STAGE only, the pinned slot is untouched."
              exit 1
            fi
            unzip -q "$STAGE/flutter.zip" -d "$STAGE"
            # Stamp the staged tree with the host arch BEFORE the
            # slot-in (gh-1736): ensure_arch can later tell a healthy
            # slot from a wrong-arch one and self-heal it instead of
            # re-exporting an unrunnable SDK on every run.

restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

DEST="$SDK_ROOT/$VER"

        # gh-1736: the archive is picked per HOST arch — the arch-less
        # flutter_macos_<v>-stable.zip is the X64 build, and an x64 dart
        # cannot exec on this Apple-silicon runner ("Bad CPU type in
        # executable", exit 126). Both matrix legs run on this ONE host
        # and share the slot (the matrix arch only steers
        # FLUTTER_XCODE_ARCHS), so the slot's SDK must match uname -m.
        # Same resolution subosito/flutter-action performs from the
        # platform arch; the naming lives in the tested sdk_slot.py.
        HOST_ARCH="$(uname -m)"
        ARCHIVE="$(python3 "$SLOT" archive "$VER" "$HOST_ARCH")"
        echo "host arch $HOST_ARCH -> $ARCHIVE"

        # Self-heal before trusting a non-INSTALL verdict: a marker can
        # point at a version dir that a human or disk cleanup removed.
        # Without this the SKIP path would export a PATH entry with no
        # flutter binary under it and every later step would die at
        # `flutter --version` until someone deletes the marker by hand —
        # the brick the #357 review flagged on the old swap. gh-1736
        # adds the arch half: a slot unpacked from a wrong-arch archive
        # (or unstamped, like the poisoned runner slot this fixes) is
        # pruned by ensure_arch and reinstalled from the right archive.
        if [[ "$DECISION" != INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ ! -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER is missing from $SDK_ROOT — reinstalling"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          elif [[ "$(python3 "$SLOT" ensure_arch "$DEST" "$HOST_ARCH")" == reinstall* ]]; then
            echo "pinned $VER at $DEST is not usable on $HOST_ARCH — reinstalling from the correct archive"
            DECISION="INSTALL $VER"
          fi
        fi

        if [[ "$DECISION" == INSTALL* ]]; then
          if [[ -d "$DEST" ]]; then
            echo "Flutter $VER already installed by a concurrent leg — reusing it"
          else
            echo "Downloading Flutter $VER (spec: $SPEC, host $HOST_ARCH) — one-time per pinned version..."
            STAGE="$(mktemp -d "$SDK_ROOT/.stage.XXXXXX")"
            # --max-time bounds EACH transfer, --retry-max-time bounds
            # the whole retry cycle: a wedged ~1GB download can never
            # hang the job until GitHub's ceiling kills it. (Same
            # pattern as the bounded asset downloads in build-macos.)
            if ! curl -fL --retry 3 --retry-all-errors --retry-delay 5 \
                --max-time 600 --retry-max-time 900 \
                -o "$STAGE/flutter.zip" \
                "https://storage.googleapis.com/flutter_infra_release/releases/stable/macos/$ARCHIVE"; then
              echo "::error::Flutter SDK download for $ARCHIVE failed after retries (bounded: --max-time 600 per attempt, --retry-max-time 900 total). The runner's network or storage.googleapis.com is unhealthy — check and re-run; partial state stayed inside $STAGE only, the pinned slot is untouched."
              exit 1
            fi
            unzip -q "$STAGE/flutter.zip" -d "$STAGE"
            # Stamp the staged tree with the host arch BEFORE the
            # slot-in (gh-1736): ensure_arch can later tell a healthy
            # slot from a wrong-arch one and self-heal it instead of
            # re-exporting an unrunnable SDK on every run.

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was

      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # Duration-balanced shards (issue #177 AC3): scripts/test_shards.json
      # maps test FILES to shards (file-level units — test/cli alone was
      # half the suite's runtime and undivisible as a dir-unit); rebalanced
      # weekly by shard-rebalance.yml from junit durations. Bootstrap here
      # is filecount-balanced; the first weekly junit rebalance converges
      # to duration balance. Unknown test files are bin-packed in at
      # runtime by shard_files.py, so a PR adding one never silently skips
      # it. The json file-reporter (converted to junit below — dart test
      # has no built-in junit reporter) feeds the rebalancer real durations
      # (issue #194 AC3).
      - name: dart test --coverage (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'
        run: |
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }})
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          mkdir -p test-results
          dart test --coverage=coverage --exclude-tags integration \
            --file-reporter="json:test-results/dart-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.

## gh-1736 — [daily-publish] cli leg failed: FIXED

**Root cause:** `.github/actions/setup-flutter-selfhosted/action.yml` downloaded the pinned Flutter SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per the official `releases_macos.json` that archive is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon self-hosted runner (`macos-m5`) and share a single SDK slot, so the slot received an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host → `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring (it is the step's own echoed script text; the log shows the download/flip succeeded and `flutter --version` died next). Worse, the poisoned slot self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` forever.

**Fix (minimum, root-cause only):**
- `sdk_slot.py`: new pure `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive (manifest-convention naming: `_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64) and `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` (prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched → `reinstall`).
- `action.yml`: resolves the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with `.fah-arch` before the atomic slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricks the runner with no manual cleanup. `build-mobile.yml` (same action/slot) inherits the fix.

**TDD:** 7 new behavioral tests + 1 structural guard added to `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`; verified RED before the fix (0/8 passing), GREEN after. End-to-end simulation of the poisoned-slot heal flow validated the action's shell logic.

**Verification:** targeted suite 25/25 pass; full suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration` = **11540 passed, 11 skipped (machine-gated), 0 failed, exit 0**; `dart analyze` clean; action.yml parses as YAML and its embedded bash passes `bash -n`; `py_compile` on sdk_slot.py clean.

**Outputs:** `outputs/rca.md`, `outputs/response.md`. Working tree clean (harness auto-save committed the changes; only the 3 intended files differ from base `e53badd`).

{"content":"### Root Cause
- The `Setup Flutter environment` step downloaded the pinned SDK from the arch-less `flutter_macos_${VER}-stable.zip` URL — per `releases_macos.json` that is the **x64** build. Both `build-macos` matrix legs run on the ONE Apple-silicon (`macos-m5`) runner and share one SDK slot, so the slot got an x64 `dart` that cannot exec on the arm64 host: `Bad CPU type in executable`, exit 126. The ticket's "download failed after retries" signature is a red herring — it is the step's own echoed script text; the download actually succeeded.
- The broken slot also self-perpetuated: the marker read `3.47.7` and the dir existed, so `resolve` answered `SKIP` and the self-heal only triggered on a *missing* dir.

### Fix
- `sdk_slot.py`: new `archive VERSION HOST_ARCH` primitive resolves the manifest-convention archive name (`_arm64` infix on arm64, none on x64); new `ensure_arch DEST HOST_ARCH` prunes a slot whose arch stamp is missing/mismatched.
- `action.yml`: picks the archive from `uname -m`, stamps each staged tree with the host arch before the slot-in, and self-heals a wrong-arch/unstamped slot into a reinstall — un-bricking the currently poisoned runner slot with no manual cleanup.
- `build-mobile.yml` (same action, same slot) inherits the fix automatically.

### Test Coverage
- `test/setup_flutter_selfhosted_test.dart`: 7 new scenario tests (archive naming, ensure_arch ok/reinstall paths) + 1 structural guard (download must be host-arch qualified); all failed before the fix, all pass after — 25/25.
- Full suite: `dart test --exclude-tags integration` — see results below.

### Notes
- Concurrent-leg safety unchanged: both legs share the host arch, so a wrong-arch prune can never remove a tree the sibling leg installed; the loser converges on the winner's stamped slot.
- First fixed run re-downloads the SDK once per arch correction (~1 GB, bounded retries), then returns to subsecond reuse.
